title: Post-build authorization record, v1
description: The verdict of the post-build authorization gate. It states that a SPECIFIC set of staged platform child manifests, produced by ONE workflow run from ONE source revision and scanned against ONE frozen vulnerability database snapshot, are eligible to become inputs to an immutable release-candidate manifest. It authorizes NOTHING ELSE. In particular it is not a statement that the images may be published publicly, that they are stable-release approved, that they carry a release signature, that the architecture set is complete, or that any other run, revision, digest or database snapshot is covered. `authorization_scope` is an enum with exactly one member for that reason: a generic boolean such as {"authorized": true} invites a later consumer to read whatever authorization it happens to need into a record that never proved it.

repository.description: owner/repo that produced this record. A consumer must refuse a record from another repository.

source_revision.description: Full source revision the children were built from. Every child's evidence must agree with this.

workflow_ref.description: The canonical producing workflow, pinned. Recording whatever the caller happened to be run as would let a branch copy of this workflow emit a record that looks authoritative. A consumer must STILL verify the run through the GitHub API: this field says what the record claims, and an in-record constant cannot prove itself.

trivy_db_snapshot.description: The ONE vulnerability database snapshot every child was evaluated against. Ten jobs each resolving their own database would let a single record combine findings judged against different knowledge states, so the aggregate requires every child to report this identity verbatim.

identity.description: Canonical snapshot identity (database digest plus its recorded update time).

frozen.description: Always true. A record whose database was not frozen for the run cannot be authorized.

staging_package.description: The private quarantine package every child was pushed to. Children referencing any other package are refused.

expected_matrix.description: The COMPLETE set of children this record claims to cover, declared before evaluation. Completeness is checked against this rather than against whatever happened to be collected, so a silently missing job cannot produce a smaller passing record.

authorization_scope.description: The ONLY scope this record can carry. It means: these exact staged child digests are eligible to become inputs to an immutable release-candidate manifest. It does not mean publicly publishable, stable-release approved, release-signed, architecture-complete, or applicable to any other run, revision, digest or database snapshot.

public_exposure_authorized.description: Always false in v1. Public exposure is authorized by a separate protected path, never by this gate. Encoded as a const so a record asserting otherwise fails schema validation rather than being interpreted.

refusals.description: Every reason the verdict is FAIL. Present and non-empty whenever verdict is FAIL.

build_created.description: The org.opencontainers.image.created value every child was built with, frozen once for the run. Repository metadata such as updated_at is not evidence of when these images were built.

image_label.description: Canonical image identity, e.g. php-fpm/8.3 or nginx/prod.

digest_reference.description: Immutable by-digest reference. A tag-only reference is refused: a tag is mutable and cannot identify what was evaluated.

tag_resolved_digest.description: The digest the registry serves for staging_tag, resolved independently. Must equal manifest_digest; a local build record is not registry evidence.

config_architecture.description: Architecture read from the pushed image config. Must agree with `platform`; a child labelled one way and built another is refused.

evidence_sha256.description: Checksum of this child's evidence directory, recomputed by the authorizer from the copied evidence rather than trusted as reported. A well-formed but incorrect value is refused.

manifest_media_type.description: Read from the registry object itself. An index digest is REFUSED: an index can still be pulled with --platform, inspected and scanned, so every downstream check would pass while the record described the wrong object. Disabling sbom/provenance makes an index unlikely, not impossible.

then.description: A PASS verdict cannot coexist with a failed child gate. Previously the verdict enum and the child gate enums were independent, so a record could assert PASS while carrying children whose smoke, scan, reconciliation and metadata all read FAIL.
A FAIL verdict must say why. The prose said refusals were present on FAIL; nothing required it.
